attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his Substack post, describing the TED exchange in his own voice.

semantics.note: The proposition keeps 'appeared to be' and the hedge 'presumably' on licensing. It leaves out 'on Friday', but the contract restores that date. This is a past-tense observation.

contract.note: The plain reading is ordinary and fair: the output only needs to recognisably resemble Peanuts, and the hedged licensing point is correctly left unscored. Nothing turns on a stretched interpretation.

evidence.note: A secondary transcription published two days after the event. It has Anderson saying he asked the OpenAI tool to imagine Charlie Brown as an AI and showing the result, in the context of GPT-4o image generation.

A contemporaneous account published 2025-04-21. It names ChatGPT as the source and describes the four-panel cartoon as Peanuts-style art with Charlie Brown and Lucy look-alikes, which establishes the recognisable appearance.

reviews.rationale: Two independent secondary accounts of the 11 April 2025 TED exchange agree that Anderson showed a cartoon he had generated with OpenAI's tool. It depicts Charlie Brown and Lucy look-alikes in Peanuts style. This meets the support condition. Licensing was hedged, so it is not scored. The packet contains no counterevidence. The accounts label the product slightly differently, but both identify it as OpenAI's, which is the scope of the claim.
